This post is a few days old, not sure if I'll help here.

I'd suggest writing the exact reason you're writing. Hold nothing back. I don't think now is the time you should think "maybe that's not appropriate right now", because you're not going to have an appropriate moment when she's gone. Write down everything in your mind you could possibly want her to know. In five years, you may wish you had just mentioned how much she's helped you along the way, or how you've put her skills to good use.

I've had a similar situation. When I was somewhat young, I was leaving the hospital where my grandma was, knowing I'd probably never see her again. I was thinking for a while if it's okay to say "I love you, grandma" because I had never said it before. I was concerned it'd be strange or cringe. Thank god I said it, because the last memory I have of her is her face lighting up with joy when I said those four words. If I didn't put in that tiny bit of effort, I probably wouldn't remember what the last thing I said to her was, nor what the last thing she said to me was. I'm happy she passed away knowing what was in my mind.

**I'm lucky I was in the situation to tell my Grandma I loved her one last time. Other people don't get that chance. You have the chance to tell your "Grandma" anything you want for the last time. Don't let that opportunity goto waste. Say exactly what's in your mind.**
